explanation: A loop repeats a block while a condition is true. Understand the starting value, what changes on each iteration, and what makes the condition become false.
exampleExplanation: n starts at 1, then increases after each loop body. The loop ends when n reaches 4.
misconceptions: A while loop checks the condition before its first iteration. A do-while loop checks afterward.
Check whether your upper bound is included or excluded. An extra iteration can go past an array boundary.

reference.title: Local C reference on loop control
reference.text: A for loop has initialization, test, and update clauses. A break ends the innermost loop or switch. A continue skips to the next iteration step of the innermost loop.
